numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For a sparse subtype that cannot hold NA (e.g. Sparse[int64, nan]), cumprod, cummin and cumsum(skipna=False) accumulate the NA gaps as real 0/False values, giving wrong numbers. A RuntimeWarning 'invalid value encountered in cast' also leaks.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The result should match the dense computation: NA gaps stay NaN and propagate as the dense accumulation does, e.g. [1.0, nan, 5.0, nan] for cumprod.
trigger_conditions: SparseArray subtype is int64, uint8 or bool with a NaN fill value (e.g. Sparse[int64, nan]), so NA gaps cannot be held by the subtype
Accumulation via cumprod, cummin or cummax on the sparse-backed Series
cumsum with skipna=False; cumsum with skipna=True takes the numeric fast path and is not affected
_accumulate densified with to_dense() instead of _densify(), which casts the fill value into the subtype

input_output_examples.input: arr = pd.arrays.SparseArray([1.0, np.nan, 5.0, np.nan]).astype(pd.SparseDtype("int64", np.nan)); ser = pd.Series(arr); list(ser.cumprod())
Same arr and ser as above; list(ser.cummin())

numerical_characteristics.dtype: Sparse[int64, nan] (also Sparse[uint8, nan] and Sparse[bool, nan] named as subtypes that cannot hold NA)
category_specific_evidence: Special value involved is NaN: the gaps of a Sparse array with fill value NaN are NA, but for a subtype that cannot hold NA, to_dense() casts the fill value into the subtype so gaps arrive at na_accum_func as 0/False and are accumulated as real values.
Where NaN enters: SparseArray._accumulate densified via to_dense() (np.asarray(self, dtype=self.sp_values.dtype)), casting the NaN fill value into the integer/bool subtype.

Correct handling: use _densify(), which promotes an NA fill value with maybe_promote rather than casting it into the subtype; the result dense values should be [1.0, nan, 5.0, nan] for the reproducer input.

Reproducer: SparseArray([1.0, nan, 5.0, nan]).astype(SparseDtype('int64', nan)); cumprod gives [1, 0, 0, 0] (expected dense [1.0, nan, 5.0, nan]); cummin gives [1, 0, 0, 0] (expected [1.0, nan, 1.0, nan]); cumsum(skipna=False) gives [1, 1, 6, 6] (expected [1.0, nan, nan, nan]).
Leaked warning: a RuntimeWarning 'invalid value encountered in cast' appears from the same cast.
cumsum(skipna=True) escapes the bug because the numeric fast path returns before densifying; the 'and skipna' gate is why skipna=False is affected.

Test expectations: for cumsum with skipna=True result subtype is int64; otherwise result promotes to float64 with Sparse NaN fill; bool subtype cumprod/cummin/cummax promotes to object dtype SparseDtype(object, nan).
Signed zero, infinities and subnormals are not mentioned in the passages.
reproduction_risks: Comparing via result.sparse.to_dense() or to_dense() reproduces the same cast-the-gaps bug; tests should compare after astype('float64') instead.
cumsum skipna=True takes a fast path and keeps the int64 subtype, so it will not reproduce the bug.
Result dtype differs by operation (int64 vs float64 vs object), so assertions on dtype must match the operation and skipna value.
Fix is unreleased (GH#68187); the wrong values did not ship, so no prior released behavior is documented.
